After breakfast, meet your English-speaking guide in the hotel lobby for a sightseeing tour of Bogotá's historic centre.

See colonial churches, old streets and squares, and architectural landmarks from the 17th to the 19th century. The old quarters sit alongside modern districts with high-rise buildings, cafés, restaurants and shops.

One of the main stops is the Gold Museum. Its collection focuses on the pre-Columbian era and includes gold masks, diadems, bracelets, ritual figurines and emblems of power. Ancient cultures associated gold with the energy of the sun and gave it special significance in rituals.

Then take the funicular up Monserrate, a hill about 3,200 metres above sea level, for panoramic views of Bogotá. The 17th-century San Vicente Monastery stands at the summit.

The tour continues at the museum dedicated to Fernando Botero, the renowned Colombian painter and sculptor. Afterwards, have lunch at a restaurant before returning to the hotel to relax.
Street performers on stilts in front of the cathedral on a square in Bogotá, Colombia
Bogotá: performers in brightly coloured costumes on the square in front of the cathedral

After breakfast, meet your English-speaking guide and leave Bogotá for a full-day trip. The first stop is Lake Guatavita, about 57 km from the capital, at an elevation of roughly 3,100 metres.

The lake is associated with the legend of El Dorado. During a ritual, a new cacique would travel by raft to the middle of the lake and immerse himself in the water while his companions threw gold figurines, known as tunjos, into the lake. Guatavita later attracted successive treasure hunters hoping to find gold on the lakebed.

From the lake, continue to Zipaquirá, a drive of about an hour and a half. The main stop is the Catedral de Sal, a cathedral carved out of rock salt about 180 metres underground. After visiting the cathedral, there is time to walk around Zipaquirá and buy souvenirs.

After the tour, have lunch at a restaurant, then return to Bogotá and transfer to your hotel.
